note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 137 to 153 - Lenton Road, Cavendish Crescent South, Clumber Road, North Road and Newcastle Circus.** Transcribed by A. Hagues as the images came in.

**Four 1871 households reappear here, all of them having moved.** **Benjamin Dowson** the solicitor, on The Ropewalk in 1871, is at 4 Clumber Road with the same nurse, Emily Drinkwater, and five more children - including twins. **Adolph Hesse**, a Hanover merchant on Western Terrace in 1871, is at 6 Clumber Road, he and his Belgian wife both exactly ten years older. **Robert Thorpe** the solicitor has come from Clinton Terrace to Cavendish Crescent South. And **John Edward Ellis**, who was managing coal mines at 29 on Derby Terrace in 1871, is on North Road at 39 as a **coal owner and bank director** - the man who became MP for Rushcliffe and Under-Secretary of State for India. See [[john-edward-ellis-in-the-park]].

**Clumber Road cannot be filed at all.** The page gives 1, 4 and 6 Clumber Road; the record holds Clumber Road East and West only by house name - Adam House, Edale House, Jelenice, Penrhyn House, Westwood, St Helier, Holly Lodge, Linden House, Felixstowe - and no numbers. **Nine named houses and not one number**, against a page that gives numbers and no names. The two cannot be matched without a third source. See [[clumber-road-names-against-numbers]].

**The Elms, Newcastle Circus** is a house name the record does not hold, and its one occupant - Elizabeth Lyman, widow, 57, property holder - lives there alone.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source. Repeated names carry a birth year and are matched on it.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book RG11/3367, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 137 to 153, transcribed by A. Hagues.
